clue.text: Report of chronicler on burial site, potentially a cracker

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words that follow are spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a chronicler is an annalist, a writer of annals, and a burial site is a crypt; in an across clue the chronicler set on the crypt follows it, giving crypt annalist

explanation.surface: A historian working on a grave site might crack a mystery of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report of' signals a sound-alike: crypt annalist, said out loud, gives the code-breaker's title. 'Cracker' means a breaker of codes, not a biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptanalyst breaks codes, so is a would-be code-cracker.

clue.text: Oily liquid cools off, covering middle of street

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around and so cover the middle pair
off here means gone bad or out of order, so the letters of cools are rearranged
the central letters of street are taken, the pair at its heart

explanation.surface: A greasy fluid on the road cools down as it spreads over the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals the anagram, 'covering' the insertion, and 'middle of' takes the central two letters of an even-length word. 'off' reads as cooling down in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Creosol is a colourless oily compound obtained from wood tar, used as an antiseptic.

clue.text: Agreed! And, if we're taking turns, I'm off

definitions.meaning: said to accept a bet or challenge

definitions.text: if we're taking turns, I'm off
definitions.meaning: when my turn ends, it is your turn to play

explanation.surface: Someone accepts a challenge and then hands over to the next player.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom accepting a wager, and literally tells the next person their turn has come.

clue.text: Engineers in open hut worried at that point

indicators.note: the corps abbreviation sits inside the rearranged letters
worried means agitated or shaken up, so the letters of open hut are scrambled

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: Army engineers fret inside a hut that has been left open, just then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' signals the anagram and 'in' the insertion; Royal Engineers is the standard crossword source of these two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereupon is a formal adverb meaning immediately after that, at that moment.

clue.text: Nile region once served up excellent cake

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up has the pieces read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written with I standing in for the figure one
a bun is a small sweet cake

explanation.surface: A former Nile kingdom once served up a first-class cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses AIBUN (A1 written AI, plus BUN), as fits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Nubia was an ancient kingdom along the Nile, in what is now Sudan and southern Egypt.

clue.text: Releasing toilet pipe

parts.note: loo is a British informal word for a toilet
to pipe is to sing in a high voice, as a bird does

explanation.surface: Letting go of a pipe from the lavatory plumbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pipe' looks like plumbing beside 'toilet', but it is a verb meaning to sing.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose is to set free or let go, so loosing is releasing.

clue.text: Twinkling finale for virtuoso part in duet

parts.note: a twinkling is an instant, a second

indicators.note: the finale is the end, so the last letter of virtuoso is taken

explanation.surface: A dazzling ending for a virtuoso's share of a duet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twinkling' reads as sparkling playing, but it is a noun meaning a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: In piano duets the secondo is the lower of the two parts, as opposed to the primo.

clue.text: Jerk stabbing Caesar's associate, maybe with passion

indicators.note: the twitch pierces the other piece, sitting inside it

parts.note: a friend of Caesar's could be a Roman ally, the maybe marking an example
a tic is an involuntary twitch or jerk

explanation.surface: A villain knifes one of Julius Caesar's friends, perhaps in a fit of passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stabbing' signals the insertion. 'Jerk' suggests a lout, but it is a twitch; 'maybe' marks a Roman ally as just one example of Caesar's associate.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting romantically means acting with ardour and amorous feeling.

clue.text: Perhaps quote too much love poetry with uniform content

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: content means contents here, so the letter sits inside the poetry

parts.note: verse is poetry
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Quoting love poems to excess, with something uniform about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' puts U inside VERSE, making VERUSE, after O for love.
explanation.definitionFit: Quoting a phrase constantly is one example of employing it to excess.

clue.text: Robin flying around church's inner passages

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the church abbreviation
flying suggests letters scattered in the air, so robin is rearranged

parts.note: CH is the usual abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A robin flits around the inside corridors of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' signals the anagram and 'around' the insertion; the bird is fodder, not a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The bronchi are the main airways branching into the lungs, internal passages of the body.

clue.text: Immobilise one cover raised in Peru's old national gallery

indicators.note: the reversed pair goes between the two outer pieces

parts.note: an Inca was a member of the people who ruled Peru before the Spanish conquest
the Tate is a London art gallery

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised has the pieces read upwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a cap is a covering or lid

explanation.surface: A Peruvian visiting an old national gallery is stopped by one lifted cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses a two-piece run, giving PACI, and 'in' sets it inside. The Tate is a famous London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To incapacitate is to disable, leaving someone unable to move or act.

clue.text: Stern composed features female's lacking

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters of features are rearranged
lacking says the letters are rearranged without the female abbreviation

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A stern woman whose composed face has lost its femininity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' and 'lacking' together ask for FEATURES minus F, giving EATURES, rearranged. 'composed' looks like calm, describing a face.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere and stern are synonyms: severe in manner, strict and unsmiling.

clue.text: An ancient Greek is charged with negativity

parts.note: Ionic describes the Ionians, a people of ancient Greece, and their dialect

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek is accused of being too pessimistic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged with negativity' sounds like an accusation of gloom; in chemistry it means carrying a negative charge.
explanation.definitionFit: An anion is a negatively charged ion, so anionic describes something with negative electrical charge.

clue.text: Most of sole behind cat's third claw

indicators.note: the trimmed word comes after the single letter
the third letter of cat is taken
most of means all but the last letter

parts.note: sole means alone, single

explanation.surface: A cat's third claw sits mostly behind the sole of its paw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' looks like the underside of a foot but means ALONE; 'Most of' trims it to ALON, which goes 'behind' T.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is a claw, especially that of a bird of prey.

clue.text: Toddlers kept engaged by this dramatic series?

parts.note: a play is a drama, used here to stand for the dramatic part
a group is a set or series of things

explanation.surface: Small children are held spellbound by a theatrical serial.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'dramatic series' is split into two words rather than read as a TV show.
explanation.definitionFit: A playgroup is a regular informal session where preschool children are kept occupied with games.

clue.text: A worthless African party originally encouraged shirking

parts.note: void means empty of value, null
the ANC is the African National Congress of South Africa

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter of encouraged is taken

explanation.surface: A useless African political party first encouraged dodging responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: Avoidance is the dodging of a duty, which is what shirking means.

clue.text: Interminable street party growing louder

indicators.note: interminable means without an end, so the last letter of the street word goes

parts.note: a crescent is a curved street of houses
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: An endless street party gets noisier and noisier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interminable' reads as endless in time, but it removes the final T from CRESCENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Crescendo is the musical term for a gradual increase in volume.

clue.text: Gives precious coat to US serviceman left wearing scraps

indicators.note: the scraps are worn by the soldier, so they go around him

parts.note: ends are leftover scraps or remnants
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An American soldier, abandoned in rags, is treated to a gilded coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts GIL inside ENDS: the soldier is wearing the scraps, so they surround him.
explanation.definitionFit: To engild is to gild, covering something with a thin layer of gold.

clue.text: Means of preserving grim impartiality

parts.note: a tin can preserves food
dour means stern, grim

explanation.surface: A way to keep a stern, unbiased face.
explanation.definitionFit: Candour once meant freedom from bias, fairness, before its sense of frankness took over.

clue.text: Variety of wine bar bottles 50 cents

indicators.note: the bar word holds the number inside it like a bottle

parts.note: to ban is to bar or prohibit
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A wine bar keeps bottles that cost fifty cents each.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' and 'bottles' look like a pub and its stock; BAN 'bottles' L, then C follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Blanc is French for white and names a style of wine, as in sauvignon blanc.

clue.text: Revered head of board removing editor

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: less means minus, with something taken away

explanation.surface: A respected chairman of the board ousts the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing' looks like the act of sacking, but it supplies LESS, as in 'five less two'.
explanation.definitionFit: Blessed means holy, worthy of reverence.

clue.text: Nutmeg's supporting commercial plugging superb college

indicators.note: in a down clue, a supporting piece goes below the one it holds up
the advert plugs a gap in the other word, going inside it

parts.note: ace means excellent, superb
an ad is a commercial
Nutmeg is the setter, so Nutmeg's means my

explanation.surface: The setter backs an advertising campaign for a top college.
explanation.walkthrough: Nutmeg is the setter's pseudonym, so 'Nutmeg's' gives MY. 'plugging' also hints at advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: An academy is a school or college for specialised study.

clue.text: Enduring stars in stage terms?

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
terms are limits or ends

explanation.surface: Long-lasting celebrities, put in theatrical jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage' suggests theatre, but it means a leg of a journey; the question mark flags the split.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a famous person whose renown lasts, an enduring star.

clue.text: More furtive adult missed by violent killer

indicators.note: the killer lacks the letter, which is taken out

parts.note: a slayer is one who kills violently
A is the film certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A sneakier grown-up eludes a brutal murderer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sly means sneaky and secretive, so slyer is more furtive.

clue.text: Moulded sink thrown away

parts.note: to sink is to decline and die away
cast means thrown, as in cast away or cast aside

explanation.surface: A shaped kitchen sink has been thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sink' looks like the basin but is a verb meaning fade or die.
explanation.definitionFit: Die-cast describes metal shaped by forcing it molten into a mould.

clue.text: Emit cry of pain close to mummy, looking rather sickly

parts.note: to yell is to emit a loud cry
ow is an exclamation of pain

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone cries out in pain beside their mother, looking a bit unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mummy' could be an Egyptian corpse or a mother; only its last letter counts.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellowish tinge to the skin suggests jaundice or illness, a sickly look.

clue.text: Whiff of sodium beginning to develop?

parts.note: Na is the chemical symbol for sodium
a whiff is a faint smell, a scent

explanation.surface: A faint smell of sodium is starting to emerge.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into being, in its earliest stage.

clue.text: I feel dry runs should be organised and easy to follow

indicators.note: organised means arranged in order, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone feels practice runs should be sorted out and simple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should be organised' rearranges I FEEL DRY RUNS; 'dry runs' sounds like rehearsals.
explanation.definitionFit: User-friendly describes something simple for people to understand and operate.
